verdict.rationale: Segment's own docs describe Data Storage Destinations that store raw Segment data in data warehouses, AWS S3 and Google Cloud Storage, and the Public API lets you manage Warehouses resources. That covers raw events landing in a customer-owned warehouse or lake. The evidence never names Snowflake, BigQuery or ClickHouse, never shows profiles being synced to the warehouse, and never mentions user-controlled sync schedules. Missing for 10: documented sync-schedule control, profile/identity data landing in the warehouse, named Snowflake/BigQuery/ClickHouse support, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, raw events and profiles land in my own warehouse or lake (Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse, S3) on a schedule I control

citations.quote: Segment offers several [Data Storage Destinations] to help you store your raw Segment data, including: Data Warehouses ... AWS S3 ... Google Cloud Storage
This includes working with resources such as Sources, Destinations, Warehouses, Tracking Plans
